<thought>The mass spectrum shows a classic carbon isotopic envelope: a dominant M peak at 114, an M+1 peak at ~6.7 % intensity (consistent with ~6 C atoms, given 13C ≈1.1 % per carbon), and rapidly diminishing higher isotopes. No 2 Da spaced peaks characteristic of Cl or Br are present, and the M+2 intensity is far lower than expected for sulfur. Therefore, carbon is the only element that can be definitively identified from the observed isotopic pattern.</thought>
<final_answer>['C']</final_answer>
